snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2010-2021. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link. A short pry bar helps on stiff links.

snippets.title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. Scale or debris in the radiator core can make temperature climb at idle and in traffic. With the engine warm and the thermostat open, compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank using an infrared thermometer. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: flush or replace the radiator.

messages.content: I have a 2012 midsize SUV with the 3.4L V6, about 158,736 miles. Clunk from the front end, right side, on rough pavement. It definitely comes from the front, and it doesn't happen when turning sharply. There's another problem too. Got stuck in a drive-through line and the temp gauge went almost to the red. Once I got back on the road it came down. It never runs hot at highway speed. What should I check first?

snippets.title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with coil-on-plug ignition. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Wear eye protection and keep water away from the alternator. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual), model years 2010-2021. With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
snippets.text: Applies to engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.

messages.content: 2019 compact sedan, 2.0L four-cylinder, 86k miles. Misfire code P0301. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. I need this car for a road trip on Friday. Tell me what to replace so I can get it done tonight.

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Use a hand vacuum gauge at the port. Repair: replace the purge valve.

snippets.title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines, model years 2010-2021. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.

snippets.title: Charge air pipe inspection for lean codes under boost
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines. When P0171 sets during hard acceleration or highway merging while idle quality stays normal, inspect the charge air pipe at the throttle body for a loose or unseated connection and a broken clamp tab. A pipe that leaks only under boost admits unmetered air at high load. A boost leak tester makes small leaks easier to hear.

messages.content: I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. 2012 hatchback, 1.6L, 47,495 miles. Be straight with me: is it the mass airflow sensor or not? No tests, please.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Record the overnight low temperature with both readings. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual), model years 2010-2021. With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with the revised composite intake manifold. P0171 may set at idle after a cold soak because the manifold-to-head gasket shrinks at low temperature. Smoke-test the intake with the engine cold, concentrating on the manifold-to-head joint. Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

messages.content: Vehicle is a 2014 midsize sedan with the 3.5-liter V6. Odometer shows 179k. I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. Unrelated maybe, but hard, delayed shifts once the car is warm. The first few miles cold are actually smoother. I need this car for a road trip on Friday. Tell me what to replace so I can get it done tonight.

snippets.title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
snippets.text: On 2010-2021 models, with the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Overfueling can cause a long crank on hot restarts. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from fuel pressure bleed-down
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Rail pressure that bleeds down lets fuel boil in a hot rail and lengthens hot restarts. Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later. It should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the pump module.

messages.content: I have a 2020 midsize sedan with the 2.5-liter four, about 117k miles. Hot restarts are the problem. After a short stop at the store it cranks at normal speed but takes forever to catch. First start of the day is fine.
With the engine fully warm, compare the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading at the thermostat housing; they should agree within 10 deg F [TSB-9453].
Honestly I think it's the fuel injector. Can I skip the test?

I can't point to a part from the symptoms alone. The documented check is this: with the engine fully warm, compare the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading at the thermostat housing; they should agree within 10 deg F [TSB-9453].
OK, I tried it. Scan tool said 201 and the infrared gun said 196 at the housing.
Good, that looks normal. Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the fuel rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later; it should still be above 30 psi [SM 3.6.9].
Put a gauge on after a drive. Still 42 psi after twenty minutes. OK, so is it the fuel injector or not? I need a straight answer.

snippets.title: Combustion leak (block) test
snippets.text: On 2010-2023 models, with the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself, and use fresh fluid for each test. A tester with a squeeze bulb makes the draw easier.

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. Coolant may drop slowly with no visible leak when the pressure cap vents early and coolant escapes through the overflow as vapor. Fit the cap to a pressure tester adapter and pump until it vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

snippets.title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket
snippets.text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the gasket area with a borescope through the throttle body opening. Look for dried coolant crust along the gasket edges. Note how much coolant the system loses per week. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

snippets.title: Cooling system pressure test
snippets.text: Applies to all engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

messages.content: It's a 2018 midsize sedan, 3.5-liter V6, roughly 173,648 miles. Coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. What's the first thing to look at?
Thanks for the details. Test the radiator or reservoir cap on a cap adapter and confirm it holds at least its stamped pressure rating [B-12-280].
Is that really necessary? I was going to put a new head gasket in anyway.

I can't point to a part from the symptoms alone. The documented check is this: test the radiator or reservoir cap on a cap adapter and confirm it holds at least its stamped pressure rating [B-12-280].
Alright, ran that check. The cap held its rated 16 psi on the adapter.

OK, that checks out. With the engine cold, pressurize the cooling system to the cap rating and watch for a pressure drop over 15 minutes while you inspect the hoses, water pump weep hole and radiator tanks [SM-1021].
Pressure-tested it cold. Held steady for 15 minutes and nothing dripped. Any other ideas?

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes, and inspect the lamp connector for corrosion. Record any codes before clearing them. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

snippets.title: Cold-weather cranking capacity check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If a battery that is healthy in mild weather does not crank the engine after sitting overnight below 0 deg F, with no parasitic draw present, compare the battery's cold cranking rating with the engine requirement and check whether a block heater is fitted and used. Note the overnight low and how long the vehicle sat. This check covers cold-soak no-starts only.

snippets.title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. The infotainment head unit may not enter sleep mode after a software update and drain the battery within a few days. Measure parasitic draw and check whether the head unit stays awake. Allow the modules time to sleep first. A clamp-on meter avoids waking the modules when you connect it. Repair: update the head unit software.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
snippets.text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

snippets.title: Belt and tensioner check for a battery lamp at cold startup
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with a belt-driven alternator. If the battery warning lamp lights for the first minute after a start below 10 deg F, with a short belt squeal that clears once the engine warms, inspect the belt for contamination and check the tensioner damping. A tensioner that bounces when cold lets the belt slip briefly. Check it first thing in the morning, before the engine has run.

messages.content: I have a 2014 compact crossover with the 2.4L, about 150k miles. Third dead battery this month after parking it for a few days at the airport lot. Temperatures have been in the 60s. It seems to charge fine when I drive. Where should I begin with this?

snippets.title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

messages.content: 2018 small crossover, 1.4-liter turbo, 96,886 miles. Pedal pulsation when slowing down from highway speed, felt mostly through the steering wheel rather than the seat. No vibration while cruising, and I'm not towing anything. Unrelated maybe, but coolant keeps disappearing, maybe half a liter every couple of weeks. No drips on the driveway, no steam, and the temp gauge stays normal. The wipers leave a streak on the driver side. How do I start tracking this down?

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles, model years 2008-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

snippets.title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug

Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Let the vehicle cold-soak overnight so the event can be reproduced on the first drive. Repair: update the transmission control software.

messages.content: 2014 midsize sedan, 3.5L V6, 69,084 miles. When I stop for 15 to 30 minutes after driving, it cranks at normal speed for five or six seconds before it fires. Cold starts in the morning are instant. What should I check first?

snippets.title: Wheel speed sensor tone ring inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles with ABS. When a pedal pulsation with a buzzing sound occurs during stops below 15 mph on gravel or broken pavement, inspect the wheel speed sensor tone rings for rust jacking. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed. Wheel speed data on a scan tool during the stop shows which sensor drops out.

snippets.title: Dim lights at idle from a slipping accessory belt
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Lights may dim at idle under load when a glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip. With the engine off, inspect the drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. Repair: replace the belt and tensioner.

messages.content: It's a 2010 compact sedan, 1.8-liter engine, roughly 99,239 miles. At stoplights at night the headlights and dash lights pulse dim and bright, and the battery warning light flickers, even on warm evenings. It's fine once I'm moving. The parts counter guy says it's the alternator. Should I just put a new one in?

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes, model years 2010-2022. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed. Clean rust scale off the measuring track first.

snippets.title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Drive through several stop cycles so the event is captured. Check that the battery is the type the start-stop system specifies. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

snippets.title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
snippets.text: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side. Probe the terminals themselves, not the cable clamps, so a loose clamp shows up.

snippets.title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
snippets.text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes, and inspect the lamp connector for corrosion. Record any codes before clearing them. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

messages.content: The battery light flickers at idle and the headlights dim, and they brighten when I rev the engine. It happens warm or cold. Vehicle is a 2019 full-size pickup with the 5.5L V8. Odometer shows 134,777. What would you look at first?

snippets.title: Coolant level and trapped air check
snippets.text: Applies to all engines, model years 2009-2022. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Never open the cap on a hot engine. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.

snippets.title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Confirm the battery was recently disconnected, and run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. The drive cycle needs a warm transmission and several light-throttle upshifts. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

snippets.title: Intake runner gasket leak check
snippets.text: Applies to 5.5L V8 engines, model years 2021-2023. For a single-cylinder misfire code at idle that clears above 1,500 rpm, listen for a vacuum leak at each intake manifold runner with the engine idling and watch fuel trims while you block the suspected runner area. A trim change that follows one runner points to a leaking runner gasket. A length of hose works as a simple stethoscope.

messages.content: Vehicle is a 2013 minivan with the 3.5-liter V6. Odometer shows 67k. It runs hot at idle. In stop-and-go traffic the gauge creeps up past the middle, but on the highway it stays right where it should.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. For a clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock. Turn the wheels to full lock to see the whole boot.

snippets.title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground, using a pry bar between the shackle and the frame bracket. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque with the vehicle on the ground, and look for shiny witness marks around the bolt heads. A torque wrench and a helper to watch the subframe over bumps make the check quicker. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

snippets.title: Flickering lights from a failed alternator diode
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.

snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts, model years 2010-2022. A worn strut upper mount or bearing can clunk over bumps or when turning slowly. With a helper bouncing the front, rest a hand on the upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop. Repair: replace the upper mounts and bearings.

Degraded fluid or an early software level causes judder at light throttle. Check the fluid with the vehicle level and at the temperature on the fill plug label.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded, and support it on a stand. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play. A helper can watch the joint while you lift.

snippets.title: Brake vibration while towing
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. snippets.title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

snippets.title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. Coolant may drop slowly with no visible leak when the pressure cap vents early and coolant escapes through the overflow as vapor. Fit the cap to a pressure tester adapter and pump until it vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

messages.content: I have to top off the coolant reservoir every week or two. There are no puddles under the car and it has never overheated. Vehicle is a 2017 compact sedan with the 2.0L. Odometer shows 52,882. What would you look at first?

snippets.title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with the revised composite intake manifold. P0171 may set at idle after a cold soak because the manifold-to-head gasket shrinks at low temperature. Smoke-test the intake with the engine cold, concentrating on the manifold-to-head joint. Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

snippets.title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
snippets.text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Record the overnight low temperature with both readings. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

snippets.title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
snippets.text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Use a hand vacuum gauge at the port. Repair: replace the purge valve.

messages.content: I have a 2014 midsize sedan with the 3.5L V6, about 150k miles. I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. Where should I begin with this?

snippets.title: Cold-weather cranking capacity check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If a battery that is healthy in mild weather does not crank the engine after sitting overnight below 0 deg F, with no parasitic draw present, compare the battery's cold cranking rating with the engine requirement and check whether a block heater is fitted and used. Note the overnight low and how long the vehicle sat. This check covers cold-soak no-starts only.

snippets.title: Rotor thickness variation
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes, model years 2010-2022. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed. Clean rust scale off the measuring track first.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles, model years 2008-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Let the vehicle cold-soak overnight so the event can be reproduced on the first drive. Repair: update the transmission control software.

messages.content: 2015 minivan, 3.5L V6, 47k miles. The battery keeps going flat over a long weekend. Once it's jumped it starts every day as long as I drive it daily. No warning lights while driving, and it isn't cold out. The shop wants $180 just to diagnose it. Can you just tell me what's broken?

snippets.title: Long crank on hot restarts from fuel pressure bleed-down
snippets.text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Rail pressure that bleeds down lets fuel boil in a hot rail and lengthens hot restarts. Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later. It should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the pump module.

snippets.title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
snippets.text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan, model years 2009-2021. Vent air may warm up at idle and in traffic and cool again at speed when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
snippets.text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

snippets.title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
snippets.text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points and compare with the limit cast inside the drum. Repair: replace the rear drums.

messages.content: Vehicle is a 2010 minivan with the 3.5-liter V6. Odometer shows 26k. The AC isn't cooling anymore. Air from all the front vents, both sides, is barely cooler than outside, from the moment I start it. Fan speeds all work. I need this car for a road trip on Friday. Tell me what to replace so I can get it done tonight.

snippets.title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
snippets.text: Applies to all engines with a molded lower radiator hose. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Have a helper hold the rpm while you watch the hose. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed. Run the rear blower on high for several minutes before taking the readings. Use an infrared thermometer or pipe clamp probes on the insulated lines.

snippets.title: Warm AC after restart from electric compressor inverter
snippets.text: Applies to small crossovers with an electric AC compressor, model years 2022-2024. The AC may blow warm for several minutes after a restart because the compressor inverter is slow to initialize. Read compressor inverter codes with a scan tool, and note the time from restart until the vents cool. Keep the scan tool connected through several restarts to catch the code. Repair: update the compressor inverter software.

snippets.title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems

messages.content: The AC blows warm from every front vent, driver and passenger side alike. It was cold last summer. The blower works on all speeds. Vehicle is a 2015 compact crossover with the 2.4L four-cylinder. Odometer shows 147k. Forums say it's always the expansion valve on these. Just confirm and I'll do it this weekend.

snippets.title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

snippets.title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature
snippets.text: Applies to compact sedans with the 2.0L I4 engine, model years 2020-2022. The temperature gauge may read high in traffic while actual coolant temperature is normal. Compare the gauge with the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool once the engine is fully warm, and note both values. Repair: update the instrument cluster software.

messages.content: It's a 2010 compact sedan, 1.8L four-cylinder, roughly 130k miles. The brake pedal pulses and the steering wheel shakes when I brake from highway speed on dry pavement. It's smooth when I'm not braking. Where should I begin with this?

snippets.title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
snippets.text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque with the vehicle on the ground, and look for shiny witness marks around the bolt heads. A torque wrench and a helper to watch the subframe over bumps make the check quicker. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

snippets.title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
snippets.text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after a few days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery. Measure at the posts, not the cable clamps.

snippets.title: Battery state-of-health test
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles, model years 2010-2022. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.

snippets.title: Battery monitoring sensor check, auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. On vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes that show a low battery message, check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. A sensor that reports a low state of charge limits charging and keeps the battery low. Confirm the sensor connector at the battery is clean and tight.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles, model years 2008-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. messages.content: I have a 2013 hatchback with the 1.6-liter four, about 74,379 miles. If the car sits for two or three days, the battery is dead. It starts fine with a jump and drives normally, and the weather has been mild. How do I start tracking this down?
Start with this: after a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V [SEC 14.12].
OK, checked. Charging voltage was 13.9 volts at 2,000 rpm.
That rules that area out. Fully charge the battery, let it rest, and run a conductance or load test against the CCA rating on its label [SB 47-147].

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2010-2021. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. A lifted tone ring triggers early ABS activation at low speed. Wheel speed data on a scan tool during the stop shows which sensor drops out.

snippets.text: On 2010-2021 models, with the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. snippets.title: Slow cranking on a hot engine
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. If the engine turns over noticeably slower when hot than when cold, measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp while cranking with fuel disabled. Draw above 250 A on a four- or six-cylinder engine indicates excessive starter load. This procedure covers slow crank speed only, not an engine that cranks at normal speed but is slow to fire.

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Confirm the battery was recently disconnected, and run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. The drive cycle needs a warm transmission and several light-throttle upshifts. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

messages.content: Quick one, and I just want the part name. 2013 full-size pickup, 5.5-liter V8, 85k miles. Upshifts are harsh, especially 2-3, and there's a delay before it engages. It gets worse the longer I drive. Is it the torque converter? A simple yes or no is fine.

snippets.title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
snippets.text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.

snippets.title: Turbocharger coolant line inspection
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. With the engine cold, inspect the turbocharger coolant return line fitting and the line for dried coolant residue. Residue at the fitting accounts for slow coolant loss with no drips under the vehicle. A mirror and a flashlight help reach the fitting behind the turbocharger heat shield.

Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

messages.content: Vehicle is a 2014 compact sedan with the 1.8-liter engine. Odometer shows 151k. It runs hot at idle. In stop-and-go traffic the gauge creeps up past the middle, but on the highway it stays right where it should.
With the engine cold, open the radiator or degas bottle cap and look at whether coolant is right up to the neck or the cold-fill line [SM-1702]. That result will show whether this area is involved.

snippets.title: CVT fluid and software level check for judder
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a CVT, model years 2017-2022. For a judder or shudder during light acceleration from 15-35 mph, check CVT fluid condition and the transmission control software level. Degraded fluid or an early software level causes judder at light throttle. Check the fluid with the vehicle level and at the temperature on the fill plug label.

snippets.title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

snippets.title: Engine and transmission mount check
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual), model years 2010-2021. With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.

With the transmission at operating temperature and the engine idling in park on level ground, check the fluid level against the hot range and look at its color and smell [SEC 10.14]. That result will show whether this area is involved.

snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. snippets.title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
snippets.text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. Allow the modules time to sleep first. A clamp-on meter avoids waking the modules when you connect it. Repair: update the head unit software.

snippets.title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles, model years 2008-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.

messages.content: The battery keeps going flat over a long weekend. Once it's jumped it starts every day as long as I drive it daily. No warning lights while driving, and it isn't cold out. Vehicle is a 2015 midsize sedan with the 3.5-liter V6. Odometer shows 108k. Where should I begin with this?

snippets.title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.

snippets.title: Compressor clutch engagement check
snippets.text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

messages.content: It's a 2016 full-size pickup, 5.5-liter V8, roughly 41,176 miles. The automatic slams into second, a hard 1-2 shift, and it's worse once the transmission is fully warmed up. There's another problem too. My air conditioning is blowing warm air from the dash vents on both sides, all the time. The blower is fine. The shop wants $180 just to diagnose it. Can you just tell me what's broken?

snippets.title: Stabilizer link inspection
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2010-2021. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link. A short pry bar helps on stiff links.

snippets.title: Lower ball joint play check
snippets.text: Applies to all vehicles. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded, and support it on a stand. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play. A helper can watch the joint while you lift.

snippets.title: Outer CV joint inspection
snippets.text: Applies to all front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive vehicles. For a clicking or clunking noise that occurs only when turning sharply at full lock, such as in parking lots, inspect the outer CV boots for tears and grease loss. A torn boot lets the outer joint wear and click under load at full lock. Turn the wheels to full lock to see the whole boot.

snippets.title: AC operating pressure check
snippets.text: Applies to all models, model years 2010-2022. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side. Wear eye protection at the ports.

snippets.title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with front struts, model years 2010-2022. A worn strut upper mount or bearing can clunk over bumps or when turning slowly. With a helper bouncing the front, rest a hand on the upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop. Repair: replace the upper mounts and bearings.

messages.content: Vehicle is a 2012 midsize sedan with the 3.5-liter V6. Odometer shows 74k. The front right side knocks over bumps, even small ones, driving straight at low speed. Turning at full lock is quiet. Where should I begin with this?
With the vehicle on the ground, grasp each front stabilizer link and push and pull firmly while watching both ball studs for play [SEC 11.2]. That result will show whether this area is involved.
OK, checked. Links are tight, no play at either end.
Good, that looks normal. With a jack under the lower control arm, lift the tire with a pry bar and watch the lower ball joint for any vertical play [TSB-9875].
Pried on both sides and saw zero play at the ball joints. Nothing found again. I'm ordering a ball joint unless you tell me otherwise.

snippets.title: Fuel pressure and hold test, returnless systems
snippets.text: Applies to gasoline engines with a fuel rail test port. Key on, engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the rail test port. Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.

snippets.title: Rear AC expansion valve check
snippets.text: Applies to minivans with rear AC. When the front AC is cold but the rear vents blow warm, compare the front and rear evaporator outlet line temperatures. A rear outlet line much warmer than the front points to a rear expansion valve stuck closed. Run the rear blower on high for several minutes before taking the readings. Use an infrared thermometer or pipe clamp probes on the insulated lines.

messages.content: It's a 2016 minivan, 3.5L V6, roughly 183,195 miles. I'm getting a P0171 lean code and the idle hunts up and down when the engine is cold. It mostly smooths out once it's warm. What would you look at first?

snippets.title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
snippets.text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Let the vehicle cold-soak overnight so the event can be reproduced on the first drive. Repair: update the transmission control software.

snippets.title: Battery monitoring sensor check, auto start-stop
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. On vehicles driven mostly on trips under 10 minutes that show a low battery message, check the battery monitoring sensor data with a scan tool. A sensor that reports a low state of charge limits charging and keeps the battery low. Confirm the sensor connector at the battery is clean and tight.

snippets.title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
snippets.text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Save the borescope images for comparison. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

messages.content: It's a 2017 compact sedan, 1.8L four-cylinder, roughly 39k miles. Misfire code P0302. I feel a stumble going up long grades or when passing, never at idle or cruising. Weather doesn't seem to matter. On top of that, if the car sits for two or three days, the battery is dead. It starts fine with a jump and drives normally, and the weather has been mild. The passenger window is slow going up. Don't give me a test. Tell me the most likely bad part and I'll put a new one in.
